notes: This file is a definition only: it is NOT executed by the agent. The main agent installs the schedule (for example as Muse cron jobs) from this document; ticket 09 creates no schedules itself. The run script is idempotent-safe: re-running a cycle never resubmits evidence, because the memory store is the source of truth for what was already submitted (ADR 0003). Quota math (free tiers only): Gemini free-tier rate limits are tight, with reported values (not Google-published) of Flash ~5 RPM / ~20 requests per day and Flash-Lite ~15 RPM / ~500 requests per day. Most work is routed to Flash-Lite (triage/extraction); drafting and judging use the strong model (Flash). The per-cycle model-call budget stays at 50, but the binding constraint is the ~20/day strong-model budget: 2 cycles/day x ~10 strong calls (at most ~5 drafting + ~5 judging, at most 5 markets/cycle) = ~20/day, which fits; a 3rd cycle/day would exceed it. Tavily: 1,000 credits/month, basic search 1 credit; a cycle does at most 5 markets x 3 searches = 15 credits, so 2 cycles/day x 19 days x 15 credits is at most ~570 credits, inside budget. Times are UTC; the competition window opens 23 November 2026 17:00 UTC and the mining window ends 11 December 2026 17:00 UTC. Scheduled runs currently run WITHOUT the OpenRouter fallback: run-cycle.sh fetches only the Gemini and Tavily credential surrogates, so a Gemini outage kills the cycle. Adding the fallback requires connecting an OpenRouter credential in the vault and extending run-cycle.sh to fetch its surrogate; the script carries a clearly-marked optional block for that, disabled until the connection exists.
